cases.expected: ValidationResult.success – no ValidationMessage objects (the instance conforms to the schema)
cases.description: When `validate` is true and the supplied JsonNode satisfies all schema constraints, walk should return a successful ValidationResult with an empty error set.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.failure – contains at least two ValidationMessage objects (type mismatch for `name` and `age`)
cases.description: When `validate` is true and the JsonNode violates the schema (wrong types), walk must collect the corresponding validation errors.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.failure – contains a ValidationMessage about additionalProperties not allowed
cases.description: Tests the branch that handles extra properties when `validate` is true and `additionalProperties` is disallowed by the schema.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success – empty error set (no validation performed)
cases.description: When `validate` is false the method should skip all validator execution and immediately return a successful result regardless of the node content.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.failure – contains a ValidationMessage indicating that the instance node is null or missing
cases.description: Ensures the null‑node guard branch is exercised; the method must treat a null instance as a validation failure.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success – empty error set (required property `age` is missing but the schema has a `required` validator that is *not* present in this particular schema configuration)
cases.description: Covers the branch where the schema does **not** contain a required‑field validator (hasRequiredValidator() returns false). The walk should succeed even though the instance is missing a property that would otherwise be required.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success – empty error set (type validator present and passes)
cases.description: Triggers the branch where the schema *does* contain a type validator (hasTypeValidator() returns true) and the instance type matches the expected type.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.failure – contains a ValidationMessage about type mismatch
cases.description: Executes the branch where a type validator is present but the instance type does not match, causing a validation error to be recorded.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.failure – contains a ValidationMessage about missing required property `age`
cases.description: The schema includes a required‑field validator for `age`. The instance omits this property, so walk must report a missing‑required‑property error.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success – empty error set (all required properties are present and satisfy their validators)
cases.description: Schema has a required validator for `name` and `age`. The instance provides both properties with correct types, so validation succeeds.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.failure – contains two ValidationMessages (type mismatch for `age` and required‑field validation still passes because the field exists)
cases.description: Schema has both a type validator (age must be integer) and a required validator for `age`. The field exists but with wrong type, so walk should report the type error while not flagging a missing‑required error.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success – empty error set (validation is disabled, even though node is null)
cases.description: When `validate` is false the method must bypass all checks and return success regardless of the node being null.
